title: Sheep's Wool Could Help Fix Broken Bones!
summary:
Did you know that sheep's wool could help heal broken bones? Scientists at King's College London made a special material from wool and tested it on rats with holes in their skulls. The material is made of keratin, a protein found in wool, hair, and nails. It worked even better than the material doctors usually use, which is called collagen.

Collagen has been used for a long time to help bones heal, but it's not very strong and can break down too quickly. Wool keratin is tougher and lasts longer. In the experiment, the wool material helped new bone grow across the holes. The new bone was more organized and looked more like healthy, natural bone. That's important because strong, well-structured bone is better at supporting your body.

Wool is also great because it's natural and often thrown away by farmers. Using it to make bone-repair material could be good for the environment. The scientists are excited because this is the first time a wool-based material has been tested in a living animal for bone repair. They hope it could one day be used in hospitals to help people heal faster and better.
why_it_matters: Finding a smart way to reuse old wool could help people heal broken bones better — and maybe someone in your family will benefit from this kind of science one day.
